newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - July bond options attract speculators.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - July bond options attract speculators.

text.p: With two days left to trade, July Treasury bond options were the focus of speculator interest in an otherwise subdued session, options traders said.

One U.S. house executed a bearish combination strategy involving the purchase of 4,000 July 112-00 puts and sale of the same amount of July 112-00 calls. The same house later sold 3,000 of the puts as bond futures climbed, working against the trade.
Separately, a dealer firm sold 2,000 July puts, also in the 112-00 strike.
The highest concentration of open interest in July options is in the 112-00 strike.

Floor traders said light buy-stops were triggered in futures as prices rose in the afternoon following a Federal Reserve coupon pass, a Fed beige book report that showed pockets of economic weakness in the nation and remarks by Fed Governor Susan Phillips that inflation has been benign.
The September bond contract finished up 9/32 at 112-05 after failing to challenge Tuesday's four-month high of 112-10.

Implied volatilities for Treasury bond options edged lower through the session, to 8.05 percent in August from 8.25 percent on the opening and to 8.30 percent in September from 8.45 percent. The late-session levels were flat to down from Tuesday.
The Chicago Board of Trade estimated total volume in bond options Wednesday at 112,000 contracts.
In the short end, implied volatility for December Eurodollars was unchanged on the day at 9.9 percent.

A Eurodollar options broker said the market's low volatility, which he attributed to the Federal Reserve's slow hand in monetary policy, was causing day traders to step to the sidelines and hedge funds and proprietary trades to dominate.
The fund-type activity shifts liquidity further out along the curve, which has a dampening effect on historical volatility and in turn implied volatility, he said.

Large trades seen Wednesday included a put tree spread in which a U.S. bank bought 5,000 December 93.75 puts and sold equal numbers of 93.50 and 93.25 puts. The trade would profit most if December futures expired at 93.50.
Other firms bought September 94.00 puts and September 94.00/93.75 put spreads in large lots.
